name: Chrono-Perception Acceleration
description: Modifies the brain's temporal processing to allow voluntary acceleration of subjective time perception — the user can 'slow down' their experience of time, perceiving events in slow motion while their body continues to operate at normal speed. In practice, this means the user has more subjective time to analyze threats, plan responses, and make decisions during fast-moving situations. A punch thrown at normal speed is perceived in slow motion, giving the user time to decide how to react — though their body still moves at normal human speed. The modification is valued by fighters, drivers, surgeons, and anyone who benefits from having more time to think during critical moments. Zheng-Dao Bioelectric's version includes an acceleration cap that prevents users from 'going too deep' — spending subjective hours in a single second, which can cause severe psychological damage.
source_organism: Synthetic neural chronoprocessor construct (no organism source)
procedure: Neural retroviral treatment targeting temporal processing centers, 8 sessions over 4 months
expression_time: 4–8 months for functional time perception shift
reversibility: Partially reversible; temporal processing never fully normalizes
side_effects: Involuntary activation during stress — seconds stretch into subjective minutes during panic
Boredom becomes excruciating — waiting in line feels like hours
Difficulty synchronizing social rhythm — pauses in conversation while processing feel normal to the user but visible to others
Rare: temporal perception locks in slow mode, trapping the user in a subjective eternity while the world moves normally around them
Emotional exhaustion from experiencing more subjective time than everyone else
social_perception: Elite and isolating. Bullet Brain users experience more life per minute than anyone around them, which creates a fundamental experiential gap. They seem distracted, slow to respond socially, or eerily calm in emergencies. Close relationships suffer from the temporal asymmetry.
story_hooks: A Bullet Brain user's temporal perception locks during a crisis — they experience hours of subjective time in seconds, watching a catastrophe unfold in slow motion with no ability to accelerate their body's response

A Slow Time user discovers that during extreme acceleration, they can perceive things that happen too fast for normal perception — electrical arcing, light flickering, micro-expressions — and what they see in those hidden moments changes everything
